Text:
Saigon Central Post Office, at 2 Cong Xa Paris, introduces the history of communication and urban architecture. A visit can move from the façade through the main hall to its historic maps, reflecting on how mail and telegraphy connected places.

The building was constructed between 1886 and 1891. Inside, the vaulted ceiling and entrance hall offer a different perspective from the exterior. Vietnam Post describes two historic maps preserved here: one shows Saigon and its surroundings in 1892; the other shows the telegraph network of southern Vietnam and Cambodia in 1936.

The maps offer complementary views. The map of Saigon and its surroundings concerns urban space; the telegraph map suggests how communication points formed a network. Together they connect the story of a single building to a larger system of communication.

First observe the hall and vault as a whole, then examine details and maps where access permits. Consider the steps a sender had to take before smartphones existed. Linking architecture to function adds meaning to the visit while keeping service areas clear.

For photographs, choose a position that leaves circulation clear and follow the hall signs. Give priority to people using postal services. On leaving, look back at the façade and connect its appearance to the spaces and functions you have just explored.
